subject: Pilot readiness: criteria, timeline & blocker registry
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Kate O'Connell <kate@novadev.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot readiness: criteria, timeline & blocker registry

Kate — thanks again for a productive discovery earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned success criteria for the 4-week pilot. Please confirm or flag edits.

Summary of call
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference runtime for NovaDev's search re-ranking use case (endpoint latency, cost/unit, and qualitative relevance).
- Scope: 4-week pilot, test dataset ~250k queries; staging -> production cutover not part of this pilot.
- Participants: NovaDev engineering + procurement; Redwood Sales + Solutions + Infra.

Proposed success criteria (high-level) — full spreadsheet attached (novadev_poc_success_criteria.xlsx):
1) Latency: P95 generation latency <= 220ms at 8 concurrent users (end-to-end, from NovaDev staging app).
2) Cost: tokenized cost not exceeding USD 0.004 per query at target throughput.
3) Quality: Re-ranking NDCG@10 lift >= 8% vs current baseline on the provided eval set.
4) Stability: No unrecoverable model-serving restarts in a 7-day continuous run.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange network details & target dataset, complete procurement kickoff.
- Week 1: Infra onboarding + baseline run.
- Week 2: Model config tuning + caching/batching validation.
- Week 3: Evaluation & metric review; begin user-acceptance checks.
- Week 4: Final report and decision meeting (go/no-go).

Ownership
- Redwood: Marcus Lin (pilot sponsor), Stephanie Nguyen (integration lead), Rishi Malhotra (infra lead).
- NovaDev: Kate O'Connell (engineering), Novadev Procurement (contract & billing).

Risks (initial) & escalation path
- Risk A: VPC peering / egress rules preventing staged traffic -> mitigation: temporary allowlist during pilot; escalation: Rishi (infra) -> Laura (CS) -> Redwood SOC lead.
- Risk B: Eval data format mismatch -> mitigation: provide simple ingestion script; contact: Stephanie.

Ask: Please confirm success criteria and assign your internal owner for acceptance tests by EOD tomorrow. I'll circulate the detailed spreadsheet and a HubSpot playbook link after I hear back.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

Attachment: novadev_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 rows)

Quick operational notes from the integration side — I'll own the app -> staging integration and orchestration of the baseline.

Immediate technical risks I see:
- Risk 1 (network): NovaDev uses a strict NGFW and our tests require a temporary allowlist for TLS egress to Redwood staging endpoints. Mitigation: use the provided network-ngfw-config.txt and coordinate change window; if not possible, we will fallback to an SSH tunnel option. Escalation: Rishi (infra) -> Laura (CS) -> Redwood SOC.
- Risk 2 (data): Your eval set includes PII fields not in the sanitized subset — please confirm whether you will provide a sanitized copy or if Redwood should run our client-side redaction script. Impact: might delay Week 1 baseline by 2 business days.
- Risk 3 (throughput mismatch): If your real-world QPS exceeds our test assumptions (8 concurrent users), we may need temporary Dedicated capacity to meet latency targets.

I'll run the baseline on Tue 05/04 after the infra call and post an issue log. If any risk becomes blocking, we'll raise SUP- ticket and mark P1 as needed.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Integration Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: criteria, timeline & blocker registry

Folks — baseline run completed this morning and uncovered a blocking issue in the KV cache warmup path for models with >64k token vocab mapping. Symptoms: repeated 500s from runtime during prefix replay which causes request queue growth.

Observed impact:
- Baseline P95 latency spikes to ~1.2s under 5 concurrent sessions (fail-to-recover loop).
- Without mitigation, this violates Success Criteria #1 (P95 <= 220ms).

Immediate mitigations (applied):
1) Disabled prefix replay caching on the staging pool (temporary, increases token compute but prevents 500s).
2) Enabled fallback model variant (quantized XLA build) for the impacted model family to avoid the buggy execution path.

Permanent mitigation plan:
- Engineering owner to push a kernel-fallback patch (ETA 72 hours) and add stronger unit tests around KV warmup.
- Add a canary rollout gate in infra; if the patch fails, we will keep fallback variant for the remainder of the pilot.

Operational asks from NovaDev:
- If you need the original latency profile (without fallback), we should consider a short Dedicated capacity window while the patch ships. Please let procurement know as this will change cost estimates.

I've opened an internal support ticket SUP-2104 and linked the run logs in the drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_PoC_plan
